question: Will any of the Magnificent 7 make an acquisition valued at $10B or more before January 1, 2027?

calls.reasoning: Base rate: Mag7 signed controlling acquisitions >=$10B EV run ~1/yr recently (Google-Wiz Mar 2025, Nvidia-Hugging Face Sep 2026; Meta-Scale 49% and Nvidia-Groq license deals don't qualify), implying ~15-20% for the ~10.5-week remaining window. Key update: FT (Oct 11, 2026) reports Nvidia in early talks to acquire Reflection AI ($25B valuation) or invest more / acqui-hire, with a deal possible within weeks; Nvidia's recent pattern (Groq, Poolside) favors license-and-hire structures that would not meet the >50% control clause. Amazon-Decart (~$7B) is below threshold; a Tesla-SpaceX merger would more likely be SpaceX acquiring Tesla (Tesla holders <50%), and is unlikely to be signed by Dec 31. No matching human prediction market found (Kalshi only prices Tesla-SpaceX merger ~60% within a year — not a match).
calls.dossier:
- Event window: after question close (~2026-10-19) -> before 2027-01-01 per criteria; as of 2026-10-19 the window is just starting (~10.5 weeks remain). Resolves off a signed definitive agreement for a controlling (>50%) stake in a target with 100% EV >= $10B (SEC filings/credible sources), not off talks, rumors, minority stakes, or license/acqui-hire deals.
- Nvidia-Hugging Face $12.9B agreement signed Sep 3, 2026 (CNBC, TechCrunch) — BEFORE the window, does not count; closing expected H1 2027.
- FT via Investing.com/Bloomberg Law (Oct 11, 2026): Nvidia in early talks to acquire Reflection AI OR increase investment; structures under discussion include full acquisition, acqui-hire + tech license, chip-supply deal, or a bigger stake. Deal 'could come within weeks' but talks are preliminary and could collapse. Reflection valued $25B (2026 round); Nvidia has invested ~$800M. Wikipedia (checked Oct 19) shows no signed deal.
- Nvidia's prior large deals used non-control structures: Groq ~$20B (Dec 2025, license + hiring), Poolside ~$7B (Aug 2026, $6B license + $1B equity) (techstartups.com, Oct 14, 2026).
- Amazon in talks to buy Decart for ~$7B (WSJ via SiliconANGLE, Oct 11, 2026) — below threshold. Amazon was also reported in April 2026 to be weighing a ~$9B Globalstar deal — below threshold.
- Tesla-SpaceX: Kalshi ~60% merger within a year (Oct 18, 2026); Barclays sees a possible December announcement, with the structure it describes being SpaceX acquiring Tesla in an all-stock deal — under this question's fine print that would count only if pre-merger Tesla holders own >50%.
- A claim on a low-quality blog of a 'Microsoft $45B CoreWeave acquisition' could not be verified; searches show no such deal.
- Reference class: Mag7 signed controlling $10B+ acquisitions — Microsoft LinkedIn 2016, Amazon Whole Foods 2017, Nvidia Arm 2020 (abandoned), Microsoft Nuance 2021, Microsoft Activision 2022, Google Wiz Mar 2025, Nvidia Hugging Face Sep 2026: about 7 in about 10 years (~0.7/yr overall, ~1/yr in 2025-26). Non-qualifying near-misses: Meta-Scale 49% (2025), Nvidia-Groq license (2025).
- Big Tech capex in 2026 is ~$650-725B, and regulatory scrutiny pushes toward license/acqui-hire structures instead of takeovers.
- Market check: no Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi market on 'Mag7 $10B acquisition' found; only the indirect Kalshi Tesla-SpaceX market.
- Searched without finding: confirmed Apple/Meta/Microsoft/Alphabet/Tesla talks for any $10B+ target as of Oct 19, 2026.

calls.reasoning: The window is short (Oct 19 to Dec 31, 2026, about 2.4 months). Magnificent 7 deals of $10B+ have historically come about once every 1-2 years, which gives roughly 10-15% for a 2.4-month window. Nvidia-Hugging Face was signed in September, before the window, so it does not count. The main upside is Nvidia's reported talks with Reflection AI ($25B pre-money). Those talks are early, and the options include a stake increase or an acquihire/licence deal, which would not count. The FT notes the licence route avoids regulatory review. Tesla-SpaceX merger talk most likely makes SpaceX the acquirer (Tesla holders about 41%), so it fails the >50% test. Amazon-Decart is about $7B, below the threshold. No matching human market was found. A traders' figure quoted by 24/7 Wall St. puts a Tesla-SpaceX announcement by year-end at 24%, but that is a different contract.
calls.dossier:
- Resolution: YES only if a Mag7 firm signs a definitive agreement for a >50% controlling stake in a target with enterprise value >= $10B (100% basis), signed after question close and before 2027-01-01. A merger counts only if the Mag7 firm's pre-merger holders own >50% of the combined company. Resolves off SEC filings or credible reports, not off rumors or talks.
- Event window: question close (~2026-10-19) -> 2027-01-01. As of 2026-10-19, roughly 0% of the window has elapsed and about 74 days remain.
- Nvidia agreed to buy Hugging Face for $12.93B (announced Sept 3, 2026; close expected H1 2027). This is BEFORE the window and does not count (TechCrunch, CNBC, 2026-09-03).
- Nvidia-Reflection AI: FT/Bloomberg (Oct 10-11, 2026) report early-stage talks. Options are a full acquisition, a bigger stake, or an acquihire plus tech licence without control. The FT says the licence route avoids lengthy regulatory review. A deal 'could be reached within weeks' but talks 'could collapse'. Reflection's last round: $25B pre-money. Nvidia has invested $800M to date (SiliconANGLE 2026-10-11; Yahoo Finance).
- Nvidia precedent: Dec 2025 Groq $20B was a licence/acquihire, not a control acquisition (background knowledge, not verified this run).
- Tesla-SpaceX: Barclays (Bloomberg 2026-10-14) says a merger could be announced before Tesla's annual meeting (by Dec 6). Proposed ~0.7 SpaceX shares per Tesla share; SpaceX ~$2.07T vs Tesla ~$1.45T, so SpaceX would be the acquirer in substance and Tesla holders would own about 41%, which fails the >50% merger test. No filings or formal talks (24/7 Wall St. 2026-10-15). Small chance of a structure where Tesla is the legal acquirer, which creates ambiguity.
- Amazon reportedly in talks for Decart at about $7B, below the threshold (techstartups Oct 2026).
- Apple internally discussed Mistral and Perplexity (2025 report, The Information); no current talks found. Meta walked away from Kalshi (~$40B valuation). Meta's $2B Manus deal was unwound in 2026 after China objected.
- 2026 is a record tech M&A year (SpaceX-xAI, SpaceX-Cursor $60B, EA take-private $55B). Mag7 deals in it: Google-Wiz $32B closed March 2026; Nvidia-Hugging Face $12.9B.
- Base rate: Mag7 $10B+ definitive acquisitions 2019-2026 include roughly MSFT-Nuance (2021), MSFT-Activision (2022), GOOGL-Wiz (Mar 2025) and NVDA-Hugging Face (Sep 2026). That is about 4 in ~7.5 years, roughly 0.5/yr (about 10-12% per 2.4-month window via Poisson). The recent rate (2025-26) is about 1/yr (about 18% per window).
- Searched and not found: any reported advanced talks for a $10B+ target by Google, Microsoft, Apple, Meta, Amazon or Tesla as of mid-Oct 2026. No Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold contract matching this question was found (one Tesla-SpaceX announcement market exists, but it is a different contract).

calls.reasoning: Base rate of Mag7 controlling $10B+ definitive acquisitions ~0.5-1/yr gives ~10-12% for the ~73-day window. Main upside is Nvidia-Reflection AI ($25B valuation): FT says a deal could come within weeks, but structures include non-control stake/acquihire+license, which Nvidia has favored (Groq, Poolside) to avoid regulatory review; ~50% some deal by Dec 31 x ~35% control structure ≈ 17%. Tesla-SpaceX likely fails the >50% Tesla-holder test (~2%). Amazon-Decart ~$7B is below threshold. No matching human market found.
calls.reconciliation: Disputes: (1) whether Nvidia-Reflection talks have advanced or been signed since Oct 10-11 FT report — searches show all coverage still traces to the FT report; talks early, no terms, no comment, options include non-control structures; Reflection valued $25B so a full takeover would qualify. (2) whether any other Mag7 $10B+ deal was announced in October — broad search found none. (3) Judgment on Nvidia choosing a control structure: Groq/Poolside precedent and FT's regulatory note favor license/acquihire; I take ~35% control conditional on a deal, ~50% deal by year-end. (4) Tesla-SpaceX: valuations imply Tesla holders ~41-42%, failing the merger test; ~2%. (5) Background rate ~10-12% for the window. Combined ≈ 0.25; Run 3 underweighted Reflection, Runs 1-2 slightly overweighted it given the structure preference. No matching human market found.
